central_question: Can interactive borderline examples help people specify a subjective visual category more consistently than a zero-shot instruction?
claims_and_limits: Google's November 4 blog explains a CVPR 2026 research method, rather than a newly launched product.
Authors report 18 roughly 90-minute sessions across healthy-food and pay-to-play tasks, with better performance against selected baselines and lower reported burden.
Small task-specific study; no universal performance guarantee or independent replication. Illustrated food judgments are conceptual, not a published dataset.

visual.shared_motif: Light violet reviewer and ambiguous food images; paired infographic explains concept scoping, borderline cases, rule revision and testing.
visual.status: Illustrative category examples, not study stimuli or medical/nutritional guidance.
